idiom_name: the Minitest::Test instance answers the collaborator message directly (duck typing)
implementation_notes: Ruby resolves collaborator calls by message, so the test instance can define the callback method and be installed as the collaborator -- method(:on_event) turns it into a Method object, and nothing has to be declared because duck typing means the SUT only cares that the message is answered. A fresh Minitest::Test instance is created per test, so instance variables used for recording are naturally per-test. When the SUT only needs a callable, a lambda or a Struct subclass defined inside the test method is the lighter Inner Test Double, and Minitest::Mock or mocha takes over when expectations, call counts and argument matching are the point of the test.
code_sketch:
class PublisherTest < Minitest::Test
  def on_event(e) = (@seen ||= []) << e          # the test answers the message

  def test_publishes_once
    Publisher.new(method(:on_event)).change("x")  # install the test's own method
    assert_equal ["x"], @seen
  end
end
pitfalls: method(:on_event) or a Proc built from the test instance keeps it alive; a background subject holding the callback can fire after teardown and mutate a finished test.
Minitest creates a fresh instance per test method, but listeners kept in class variables or constants are shared across the suite and leak state.
Duck typing means a typo in the callback name fails only when the SUT calls it, so always assert on the recorded values rather than assuming the callback ran.
